item.title: What is the Rutgers quarterback situation entering Michigan game?
item.description: PISCATAWAY – In a season filled with quarterback questions, now Rutgers football is facing another . Who will start this week’s game against Michigan? That’s the newest question and it’s relevant after starter Dylan Lonergan suffered an injury early in the Scarlet Knights ’ 42-14 loss to Northwestern on Oct. 24, and whether he’ll be able to play remains unclear. Schiano said Tuesday, Oct. 27 that he will leave Lonergan’s status to the availability report, the first of which is released Wednesday night. It was the second game this season that Lonergan had to leave because of an injury – he also missed the team’s game against Boston College (the second game of the season) because of the injury he suffered in Week 1 in the loss to UMass. It’s been a disappointing campaign so far for Lonergan, who was showing signs of improvement and played his best game as a Scarlet Knight in the Oct. 17 win over Maryland. “I’m disappointed and sad for the kid because this means so much to him and he puts so much of himself into it,” Schiano said. “To have to leave the game now for the (second) time, yeah it’s killing him. And I’m sad for us because he really was coming on. You could see it against (Southern California) and you could see it at Maryland. You could see him really coming on. Injuries are part of football. It’s a violent game.” If Lonergan can’t play, then Rutgers has to look to AJ Surace or Sean Ashenfelder. Surace again struggled after coming in for Lonergan, going just 7-of-18 passing for 64 yards with one interception against Northwestern. Seeking a spark in the second half, Schiano called on third-stringer Sean Ashenfelder, who went 2-of-9 for 36 yards. Ashenfelder hasn’t even gotten many practice reps, partially because the bulk of them in even in training camp went to Lonergan and Surace as they battled for the job. Schiano reiterated again Tuesday that once the season starts, there are even fewer reps to go around. Surace is in his third year with the program and he just hasn’t played well enough in the chances he’s gotten so far this season. Schiano, though, has liked how Surace has battled through the adversity. He’s still confident in Surace’s ability. “AJ’s a fighter,” Schiano said. “He’s not happy with the way he’s played. But he came out in practice like the national championship’s around the corner. That’s the way he approaches everything he does. If you’re going to bet on a guy, probably bet on him.” This article originally appeared on Asbury Park Press: What is the Rutgers quarterback situation entering Michigan game?

item.title: Enduring memories and 'imposter syndrome' - The GAA Social meets Mayo star Carney
item.description: Jack Carney's inspirational displays in the Mayo midfield has earned him a Footballer of the Year nomination [Getty Images] Jack Carney has two enduring memories from the whirlwind of celebrations that followed Mayo's return to the promised land after 75 years. Both are linked to places that helped shape him. He will never forget seeing the crowd of people that waited at Kilmeena - his home club - to see their heroes bring Sam Maguire onto their patch. Kilmeena was the last stop on the All-Ireland champions' homecoming parade, as Andy Moran's side were roared Running behind schedule, when the bus finally arrived, Carney was struck by the numbers that stuck around to see one of their own. "To see the amount of people that waited there just to see the team, to see Sam Maguire returning to such a small club, no-one ever thought it was possible," Carney tells Thomas Niblock and Oisin McConville on the GAA Social. "To finally bring it back there to my local people was something I'll never forget." Jack Carney- Winning the All-Ireland with Mayo 'This is something different here' The other memory Carney hopes proves ineradicable is the powerful feeling that accompanied carrying Sam onto Achill Island alongside team-mates Donnacha McHugh and Diarmuid O'Connor. Carney has deep family roots on the island. His father and grandfather hail from there and both were present as Carney, McHugh and O'Connor - soundtracked by more than 100 bagpipers, including his father - carried the famous trophy across the Michael Davitt Bridge and onto the island. Given his connection to Achill, the power and significance of the moment was not lost on Carney. "According to my father and grandfather, that's never happened before [bringing Sam Maguire on to the island], so I recognised the cultural importance of it - and you could feel it," says Carney. "That originally wasn't on the calendar as a club until further down the line. The island empties when summer is over. People return to where they're from originally, Dublin or Galway or wherever, and I really wanted to get the trophy down there while the island was vibrant and alive. "My grandfather was the sergeant on Achill Island. My father grew up in the barracks and the GAA pitch was the back garden. They kind of claim me as half one of their own." Carney, whose two-point score launched Mayo's All-Ireland final comeback against Kerry, added: "With no Achill player on the team, it was really important that both myself and Donnacha - both our fathers are from there - to get down there and show our appreciation for what they've done for us and our families. "And Diarmuid O'Connor just has a sense of knowing when something will be good and when to be there. "He came down with us and I'm delighted he was there because someone who didn't really understand the weight of it all - when we were crossing the bridge, he could say he could just feel it, he said, 'this is something different here'." item.title: Twenty-seven WASC swimmers combine for 57 first-place finishes in meet
item.description: WATERTOWN — The Watertown Area Swim Club Dolphins kicked off what they hope will be another very successful short-course season in 2026-27 by hosting the Ghouls in the Pool meet. The one-day meet was held on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in the Prairie Lakes Wellness Center's indoor pool. The home meet was the first of four scheduled home meets this season for the Dolphins , who have finished second in the State Class A Short-Course Championships each of the past 10 years and second in the State Class A Long-Course Championships eight years in a row. Watertown also has regular-season meets scheduled at the PLWC on Dec. 4-6 (2026), Jan. 16-17 (2027) and Feb. 5-7 (2027) before hosting the State Class A 12-and-Under Championships on Feb. 26-28 (2027). The State Class A 13-and-Under Championships are slated for March 4-7 (2027) at Pierre. WASC Girls Fourteen female swimmers combined for 29 first-place events in the Ghouls in the Pool meet. Collins DeBoer (ages 11-12), Marie Makens (6-and-under) and Sydney Sparks (17-19) each won four races. Charlotte Holien (13-14) and Haevyn Jones (13-14) each won three races and Amelia Erickson (9-10) and Essence Hinkelman (11-12) each two. Other event winners were Gracie Anderson (11-12), Everlie Fischbach (13-14), Justine Kranz (15-16), McKenzie McKeever (7-8), Harper Meidinger (17-19), Josephine Waite (15-16) and Jada Leigh Wellnitz (15-16). Leading the way for WASC was Griffen Gerrish (6-and-under) with four wins and Flynn Erickson (7-8), Clayton Muller (13-14) and Cooper Smith (15-16) with three apiece. Paul Feist (17-19), Owen Hoots (9-10), Pierce Mathiason (17-19), RJ Matthies (15-16), Brooks Melmer (7-8) and Kuper Simons (13-14) each won two races and Channing DeBoer (13-14), Rhett Ellingson (7-8), and Penn Feist (15-16) each one. item.title: Fennville's mother-daughters combo connects championship volleyball teams
item.description: FENNVILLE - When Morgan Winne played volleyball for Fennville High School, the team was strong. The Blackhawks won the SAC conference title in 2000 and 2001, winning a district championship in the latter. "It started in 2000. We had a really good team and won conference my junior and senior year. We had really good chemistry and won districts in 2001 as well. We want to strive for that this year, too," Winne said. "We have been trying to build that culture back up and we are on an upward trajectory." That trajectory has been fun for the Winne family as Morgan Winne is an assistant coach with daughters Marynn and Adelynn on the team. More: Fennville volleyball claims first SAC division title since 2001 with huge sweep More: Fennville's MacKenzie McIlwain reached unprecedented milestones no one in area history has reached "It has been really fun to see them come out of their shells and just gain confidence throughout the season," Morgan Winne said. "It is really special to have them experience what I did 25 years ago." The next generation of Winnes understand how special this opportunity is, especially with their mom getting to share in the journey. "She has been there for me and my sister, supporting us," Marynn said. "Us being together definitely creates a stronger bond." There are, of course, struggles and challenges with having a mom for a coach - and a sister for a teammate. "We definitely argue a lot because we are siblings, but that also makes us stronger. We have a strong energy together on the court," Adelynn said. "It is definitely nostalgic for her and she has helped us understand what it takes to get here. "It is challenging to be a mom and a coach. You feel like you need to be tougher on your own kids. It is hard to separate that boundary and find the balance," Morgan said. "It is very exciting to see all the hard work. We have always known it has been possible and to have them taste what it is like to win, they are understanding their potential. It is really fun to see, especially with my two girls on the team." The Blackhawks will have all three Winnes together again next year as they look to keep the momentum of the program upswing going. "It means a lot to us. We knew it was a possibility but we had to work hard and work together to get it," Marynn said. "It definitely gives us a boost for the years to come, knowing what it takes to win conference." Contact sports editor Dan D’Addona at Dan.D’Addona@hollandsentinel.com. item.title: FIA partners with AWS to help drive future F1 regulations
item.description: Motorsport photo The FIA has announced a wide-ranging partnership with Amazon Web Services as it aims to upgrade its digital capabilities. AWS will join as its Official AI and Cloud Computing Partner, as the governing body will use AWS's suite of AI tools to improve its capability to produce future technical regulations. The FIA also runs its aerodynamic simulations on AWS’s High Performance Computing technology, allowing it to conduct air flow tests in the virtual world without having to build physical parts, speeding up the process and reducing the costs involved. This partnership also expands the digital licensing platform the governing body uses to simplify tasks like licence administration, which should make it easier for national sporting authorities to run their events and for officials to sign up. That digital platform, first trialled in Canada and Sri Lanka, will now be rolled out across more countries. Sepang race start Sepang race start The AWS integration forms part of the FIA’s wider digital transformation, as president Mohammed Ben Sulayem explained. "Technology is changing every part of our sport, and the FIA must lead that change. Our new partnership with AWS will support everything from the cars of the future to the grassroots clubs where so many careers begin. "By bringing world-class cloud and AI technology into the heart of the FIA, we can make it simpler for drivers, officials and volunteers to take part, help our Member Clubs work more efficiently, and move closer to our ambition of doubling global motor sport participation." AWS is already an existing partner of F1 management, having joined in 2018 as its innovation technology partner. Among other services, AWS tools process telemetry data for broadcast use, powering live strategy predictions. item.title: Liverpool may be sleepwalking into diabolical 2027 transfer mistake – opinion
item.description: Liverpool may be sleepwalking into diabolical 2027 transfer mistake – opinion Jose Mourinho is reportedly keen on Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister. Sky Sports Germany claim that the Argentine star is high on Real Madrid’s wishlist, with the Spanish outfit paying close attention to the situation ahead of the footballer’s contract expiring in the summer of 2028. On current evidence, Liverpool should keep Alexis Mac Allister (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) There were suspicions that a truly horrendous domestic campaign from the former Brighton man would culminate in his departure from Anfield this summer. However, following an impressive (and evidently rejuvenating) World Cup campaign with Argentina, we’ve seen Mac Allister reborn in the middle of the park for Andoni Iraola’s men . In fact, there’s a pretty convincing case you could make for the 27-year-old being a strong contender, alongside Jeremy Jacquet, for Liverpool’s player of the season, as things currently stand. There were serious concerns about the midfielder’s legs being gone, given he’s endured a relentless run of fixtures between his involvement across Brighton, Liverpool and the national side. But if we’re seeing this version of Alexis Mac Allister every week, and there’s hope for some longevity beyond the end of his contract, you have to wonder whether Liverpool might be tempted to extend his current terms – even if only to protect his value. The case for selling Mac Allister to Real Madrid (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Reporting from Sky Sports Switzerland claims that Liverpool are firm on the idea that they won’t be offering their leading performer a contract extension, despite Mac Allister being more than open to extending his stay at L4. Why? Well, the Reds are reportedly planning another midfield overhaul, and so Mac Allister is presumably one name that could be sacrificed on the transfer pyre in the interest of bringing in a quality signing. There is some sense in this approach; the former Seagulls man is, currently, one of our more valuable assets. But if you’re selling a player with a year left on his contract, you’re opening yourself to being bullied on the price tag (if you’re not prepared to risk a free exit) without a bidding war, and it seems like Real Madrid are the only really keen suitors at this stage. But, realistically, what are Liverpool hoping to achieve with this? Because on current evidence, Alexis Mac Allister is the one senior midfielder who appears to have taken to Andoni Iraola’s methods like a duck to water. He sits deeper than Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, and his passing is considerably more impactful – is there an expectation that either of his teammates will improve in that regard? We all broadly agree that bringing in a more natural six would be a sound move for the recruitment team. But would selling the Argentina international really be in our best interests? item.title: Preview | Austria Wien vs Juventus Women | UWCL
item.description: Preview | Austria Wien vs Juventus Women | UWCL The UEFA Women's Champions League is back, and the Women's First Team are heading to Austria to take on Austria Wien on Matchday 3 of the League Phase. Isaac Guerrero's side lost their opening UWCL game 2-1 against Benfica. but won 3-0 away at Hacken to get the campaign off the mark on Matchday 2. Let’s get up to speed ahead of the game with the pre-match stats. INTERESTING FACTS The meeting between Austria Wien and Juventus will be their first-ever UEFA Women's Champions League match; overall, Italian teams are unbeaten against Austrian sides in the competition (W8, D3). Juventus are unbeaten in their last four UEFA Women's Champions League away games (W3, D1) after losing three in a row previously; the Bianconere's biggest away win in the competition came in their only previous meeting in Austria (5-0 against St. Pölten in December 2025). Juventus has the third-most recoveries from pressing situations in the UWCL this season (33, behind only Arsenal and Barcelona). Alba Redondo of Juventus has attempted the most shots of any player in this UEFA Women's Champions League season (14) and has scored in both of her matches in the tournament. Alba Redondo has been directly involved in 12 of Juventus' 28 goals this season, across all competitions, with nine goals and three assists (43%). UWCL | BK Häcken-Juventus Women | Gallery OPPOSITION FOCUS Austria Wien are yet to win after their first two UEFA Women's Champions League matches (D1, L1); however, they picked up their first-ever points in the competition on Matchday 2 against Italian opposition (1-1 against Inter). No team has had more different players score than Austria Wien in the 2026/27 Austrian Championship: 11 in 10 matches played, the same as St. Pölten. Among the 221 players to have attempted 25 or more passes in the 2026/27 UEFA Women's Champions League, Jasmin Pal of Austria Wien boasts the highest percentage of forward passes (78%, 53 out of 68).

item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The performance by Detroit Red Wings goalie Michal Postava in his first NHL start, as he downed Connor McDavid and the Edmonton Oilers on the road was impressive. “Postava, we’re so excited for him and happy for him,” Red Wings coach Todd McLellan told reporters after the game. “Sometimes that’s how it happens. Since 1990, only 12 homegrown goalies have made their NHL debut between the posts for the Red Wings. Postava was just the fifth among that group to earn the win in his first NHL start. On December 3, 2016, Coreau suffered a 5-3 loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins. Postava is the first Red Wings goalie to win his first NHL start in a Detroit uniform since fellow Czech goalie Petr Mrazek beat the St. Louis Blues 5-1 on February 7, 2013. Jimmy Howard (Nov. 28, 2005, 5-2 win vs. the Los Angeles Kings), Norm Maracle (March 17, 1996, 4-3 win vs. Edmonton) and Kevin Hodson (January 6, 1996, 3-0 win vs. the Chicago Blackhawks) also were winners when they made their first NHL start for the Red Wings. Chris Osgood and the Red Wings fell 6-3 to the Toronto Maple Leafs on October 15, 1993, in his first NHL start. Scott King got his first NHL start for the Red Wings on January 28, 1991, against the New Jersey Devils. He didn’t figure in the decision as Detroit lost 6-2. item.title: Dani Carvajal opens up on Real Madrid exit, Valverde, Ancelotti, El Clasico, future return
item.description: Dani Carvajal opens up on Real Madrid exit, Valverde, Ancelotti, El Clasico, future return Dani Carvajal is adjusting to life away from Real Madrid after spending 23 years associated with the club, but his emotional connection to the Bernabeu remains strong. In an interview with AS , the former Madrid defender reflected on his departure, praised Federico Valverde’s performances and identified Carlo Ancelotti as the manager who had the greatest influence on his career. Now playing for Getafe, Carvajal also discussed the possibility of returning to Madrid in a coaching role. Carvajal left Real Madrid after making 451 appearances and winning 27 trophies, having progressed through the academy to become a key first-team figure. His departure marks the end of a remarkable chapter, although he is embracing the challenge of proving himself in a different shirt. Dani Carvajal reflects on leaving Real Madrid for Getafe The defender admitted that adapting to his new routine has not been straightforward after so many years travelling to Real Madrid’s training complex at Valdebebas. “I had an incredible send-off – one of the best experiences of my life. “Going out onto the street and feeling the warmth of the Madrid fans, thanking me for everything I’ve done and asking me to come back in the future, is what fulfils me the most – more than the trophies. “Feeling that the fans are proud of how I’ve given my all is the best thing ever. Now at Getafe, I’m treating it as a challenge, and I’m really looking forward to playing.” After a career filled with silverware, Carvajal placed particular importance on the connection he built with Madrid fans. Carvajal now plays for Getafe. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Asked about the defining moments of his 13 years in the first team, he recalled the milestones that shaped his career. “The day of my presentation, without a doubt. The day of ‘La Décima’, which marked the start of a 12-year golden era with a very young squad and academy graduates like Nacho, Morata and Joselu himself. “And I’ll also always remember the day of my farewell.” Carvajal praises Valverde after Real Madrid’s El Clasico victory Despite his move to Getafe, Carvajal followed Real Madrid’s 2-1 victory over Barcelona in El Clásico with considerable emotion. He believed the match demonstrated Madrid’s determination and praised both teams for their performances. “I was nervous. I thought it was a cracking match. Both teams put in a great performance, but Madrid in particular never backed down at any point. “Real Madrid made a statement. It looks different, but I watched it wearing a Madrid shirt.” Carvajal also highlighted Valverde’s ability to contribute in different positions, particularly at right-back, where his physical qualities allow him to influence both phases of play. “He’s very versatile. Thanks to his physical attributes, he flies up and down the pitch; he’s a powerful passer and covers a lot of ground. He’s doing very well.” Carvajal

item.title: Josh Allen climbs NFL MVP rankings without even playing a game
item.description: Josh Allen didn't play a game last week. His NFL MVP stock still went up. The Buffalo Bills quarterback jumped two spots to No. 1 in NFL.com's latest MVP rankings , overtaking San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy despite Buffalo having a bye in Week 7. Allen moved from third to first in the rankings released Tuesday by NFL.com senior writer Kevin Patra. Purdy dropped to second after San Francisco suffered its first loss of the season, a 29-20 defeat against the Atlanta Falcons. Allen has been one of the NFL's most productive players through six games, accounting for a league-leading 17 touchdowns while guiding Buffalo to a 5-1 record. He has completed 66.7% of his passes for 1,504 yards, nine touchdowns and four interceptions while adding 240 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. Some of Allen's most impressive numbers go beyond traditional statistics. Why Josh Allen is No. 1 in NFL MVP rankings Allen leads NFL quarterbacks in several advanced metrics, according to NFL.com's analysis. His 0.29 expected points added per dropback ranks first among quarterbacks, as does his average of 8.8 yards per pass attempt. Allen also ranks second with a 51.7% success rate, a metric that measures how often a quarterback's plays improve his team's expected scoring outlook. Perhaps the most striking statistic is Allen's impact on winning. Allen has accumulated a 229.1% win probability added, more than 111 percentage points ahead of the next-closest quarterback. The metric measures how much individual plays increase or decrease a team's chances of winning based on the game situation. Buffalo leads the NFL in scoring at 32.8 points per game, helping overcome a defense that has allowed 28.5 points per game, which is 30th in the NFL. NFL MVP rankings entering Week 8 Here's NFL.com's top five entering Week 8: Josh Allen, Buffalo Bills: Up two spots Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers: Down one spot Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Seattle Seahawks: Previously unranked Kenneth Walker III, Kansas City Chiefs: Down two spots Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars: Down one spot Purdy led the rankings entering Week 7 after guiding San Francisco to six straight victories to start the season. But he struggled in Sunday's loss to Atlanta, completing 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Smith-Njigba moved into third after catching nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City. NFL.com listed Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff and Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams as players who could soon enter the top five. Allen, who won his first NFL MVP award for the 2024 season, is seeking to become the 12th player in league history to win the award multiple times. item.title: Game 4 World Series hero Ben Williamson shares immediate reaction to Rays’ wild win
item.description: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Game 4 World Series hero Ben Williamson shares immediate reaction to Rays’ wild win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays pulled off a stunning comeback against the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the World Series at Tropicana Field on Tuesday. The Rays beat the Brewers, 4-3 , in 12 innings to stave off elimination in the best-of-seven series. Ben Williamson was the hero for Tampa Bay, hitting a walk-off single with the bases loaded to drive in Nick Fortes for the wild victory. In the postgame interview, Williamson, who came in as a pinch-hitter, touted the Rays’ resolve and credited his teammates . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Just being ready for the situation. These guys got us in the game, kept us in the game, and to come through, that spot feels good,” said Williamson. “It just shows the resiliency of this group. We continue to fight, and that’s been the motto of this series and this whole season. Just fight.” “We continue to fight and that’s been the motto of this series and this whole season” Ben Williamson talks with @Ken_Rosenthal after he walked it off for the Rays in Game 4 of the 2026 World Series pic.twitter.com/i4QnaP8te1 — FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 28, 2026 The odds are stacked against the Rays , as no team has ever come back from a 3-0 deficit in the World Series. Only the Boston Red Sox have overcome the said hole in a seven-game series in league history. The 25-year-old Williamson delivered Tampa Bay’s first walk-off hit in the playoffs since Brett Philips did it in Game 4 of the World Series in 2020 against the Los Angeles Dodgers. According to MLB.com’s Sarah Langs, it was also the first walk-off win while facing elimination in the Fall Classic since David Freese’s home run for the St. Louis Cardinals in Game 6 of the World Series in 2011 against the Texas Rangers. item.description: Tresoldi declared "not for sale" by Club Brugge amid interest from Bayern, Arsenal, Barcelona and other European giants Club Brugge have ruled out a winter exit for Germany U21 forward Nicolò Tresoldi amid reported interest from several of Europe’s top clubs. The 22-year-old has been linked with Bayern Munich, Arsenal, Barcelona and other European heavyweights after scoring 12 goals in 14 appearances for Brugge this season. However, Belgian newspaper Het Nieuwsblad reports that an unnamed member of the club’s board has declared Tresoldi “not for sale”, ruling out a January move. The situation could change in the summer, though. If Tresoldi continues his impressive form, Brugge may find it difficult to keep hold of the highly sought-after striker. Tresoldi's contract with the Belgian club runs until the summer of 2029.

item.description: US Lecce v AC Monza - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Premier League sides Everton and Crystal Palace have been handed a major transfer boost ahead of the winter market as Italian outfit Lecce prepare to listen to offers for prized centre-back Tiago Gabriel. Despite tying the 21-year-old defender down until 2030, the Serie A club are willing to sanction his departure in the new year. Italian outfit invite winter bids According to Football Insider , Lecce have decided they are "ready" to cash in on the Portuguese defender and will sell him to the "highest bidder" when the January window opens. Both the Toffees and the Eagles are tracking the youngster closely alongside several leading Italian clubs following his impressive breakthrough campaign last season. Everton boss David Moyes wants to secure his signature despite already boasting strong depth in central defence. Portuguese prospect enjoys rapid rise Although signing a new centre-half is not a pressing winter priority on Merseyside, recruitment chiefs view Gabriel as a talent with a bright future and are ready to pounce as Lecce accept they cannot keep him long-term. As recently as the 2024-25 season, the defender was turning out for Estrela da Amadora's B team in his native Portugal before quickly becoming a cornerstone of the Italian club's senior setup. He missed the starting line-up in just two Serie A fixtures last term as Lecce narrowly avoided relegation to the second tier, and he has already recorded two goals and an assist across six league starts this season. Attacking reinforcements remain urgent priority While Everton weigh up a defensive swoop, former club chief executive Keith Wyness told the same outlet on Tuesday that recruiting a striker in January is far more urgent after missing out on a late summer deal for Folarin Balogun . That failed pursuit has left French forward Thierno Barry as the sole senior centre-forward at Moyes' disposal this season. Although the manager has handled the striker carefully so far, he lacks any alternative options up front, and Wyness believes failing to land another attacker in the summer has already cost the Merseysiders "six points" in the Premier League table. Fierce competition awaits January suitors Securing Gabriel's services in the new year will not be straightforward for Everton given the rival interest from Palace and top Serie A sides. Meanwhile, Moyes must navigate a demanding autumn and festive schedule with a thin attacking department before reinforcements can arrive. How the Toffees balance their winter budget between a much-needed striker and a long-term defensive prospect will define their upcoming transfer window.

Elite clubs are not simply searching for defenders who can head clear and win duels. They want players comfortable receiving under pressure, shifting across the line, holding their position intelligently and recovering in open space. Jeltsch appears to tick a number of those boxes. Barcelona’s interest is framed around that tactical suitability. Hansi Flick is understood to appreciate Jeltsch’s ability to operate in a pressing team with an advanced defensive line, qualities that suit the Bundesliga environment and would, in theory, translate well to his ideas. The same logic explains Liverpool’s attention. Under Andoni Iraola, Liverpool’s defensive planning will be built around mobility, aggression and players who can defend large spaces. item.title: It's over, Liverpool star now relying on €80m gamble to save career
item.description: It's over, Liverpool star now relying on €80m gamble to save career One Liverpool star appears to have no way back. He's depending on a €80m gamble to get things back on track. Liverpool have made some big decisions this season as Andoni Iraola looks to build a team out of this group. Of course, most of those decisions came in the transfer window. But we’ve seen plenty of them since the season started, too. Midfield has been a massive one - Trey Nyoni’s role in the squad continues to get stronger and stronger. Ryan Gravenberch no longer seems to have a place as the main holding midfielder, too, while Lewis Koumas is certainly the no.2 striker in the squad (at least until Hugo Ekitike reappears). But maybe one much bigger decision has been made. One that essentially calls time on one player’s Liverpool career. Jeremie Frimpong has no way back Ronald Araujo has been a revelation. We imagine the initial plan with him was to be a centre-back but fortunately, Jeremy Jacquet has been so good that it makes more sense to use him as a first-choice. That’s allowed Araujo to lock down a position at right-back. The Uruguayan isn’t a modern-day full-back in that he’s not exactly creating chances or offering much width, but he’s a rock-solid defensive force there. And that’s allowed for Liverpool to act without an overlapping player for the winger on that side. They’ve essentially got full license to attack in any way they’d like and it’s working. Rio Ngumoha and Bradley Barcola - both wingers who prefer to attack down the line on that side - have had massively positive impacts in both of Liverpool’s last two games. Having a defence-first full-back before them only helps in that. Not only that, but it’s reduced the need for a defensive midfielder. Liverpool have had more security with a defensive full-back. It also means the right-sided centre-back isn’t needed to constantly cover on that side. But this strategy means is bad news for Jeremie Frimpong . The Dutchman is essentially the opposite of Araujo - a pure attacking player who unquestionably has an effect on the winger in front of him. Having him there asks for more cover from the centre-back, too, suddenly making the need for a defensive midfielder paramount. And so it feels right now like Frimpong can only thrive at Liverpool if they do sign that defensive midfielder - and that the signing is an overwhelming success.

item.title: ‘We have to be able to…’ – JJ Redick’s blunt statement on the one thing the Lakers need after loss
item.description: Photo by Harry How/Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick had a blunt assessment of what the team needs to deliver every night to keep winning after their first loss of the 2026-27 NBA season. The Lakers fell to a 136-129 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers at home on October 27, dropping their record to 3-1 while the Blazers improved to an undefeated 3-0 on the season. The loss was marked by the Lakers being a complete mess defensively, a takeaway that head coach JJ Redick shared after the loss. JJ Redick admits the Lakers’ defence is responsible for loss to Blazers Redick spoke to the media after the game, admitting that the Lakers need to be strong enough defensively to win home games when their offence is producing 129 points on their own. “But we got good looks, and I think we have to be able to rely on our defence every night. If we score 129 points at home, we should be able to get enough stops to win.” “And credit to Portland, for sure. I said it before the game; it was going to be a great test for us because they’re a really good basketball team. They showed that tonight.” Despite the Blazers proving this season that they might be a dangerous team, the Lakers cannot be pleased with an outcome where their offensive stars delivered, but the defence completely collapsed. Shooting variance also has to be factored in, as the Blazers shot 18-for-36 from three for a 50% clip that is not sustainable over an 82-game season. Coach Redick also needs to look at the rotations he is using, as he could not find a great balance between the personnel who need to be key in games. Matisse Thybulle ended the game as a -12, while bench big Sandro Mamukelashvili was a +6. One loss does not define a season, but the Lakers already know what their biggest weakness is and have 78 more games to address that as the season goes on. item.title: La Liga president meets Chinese ambassador as Kylian Mbappe controversy continues to escalate
item.description: La Liga president meets Chinese ambassador as Kylian Mbappe controversy continues to escalate Real Madrid’s impressive victory over Barcelona in Sunday’s Clasico has been overshadowed by an unexpected controversy involving Kylian Mbappe. The French superstar’s remarks about a Chinese political figure have triggered a backlash that now extends well beyond his personal sponsorship agreements. La Liga president Javier Tebas has taken another significant step to contain the situation, holding talks with China’s ambassador to Spain. The controversy is now threatening the league’s commercial and broadcasting relationships with the country. Tebas holds talks with Chinese ambassador over Mbappe controversy On Tuesday, Tebas confirmed that he had met Chinese ambassador Yao Jing to discuss the fallout from Mbappe’s comments and explore possible solutions. “Today I held a meeting with the Chinese ambassador to Spain to address the situation caused by Kylian Mbappe’s statements and seek solutions that will allow us to overcome this episode,” Tebas explained. The controversy originated from an interview on The Bridge , during which Mbappe discussed a meme showing his face superimposed on an image of former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. The reaction has been substantial. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV suspended La Liga coverage and removed promotional material featuring Mbappe. Three Chinese companies have also ended their sponsorship relationships with the Frenchman. Tebas emphasised the importance of protecting La Liga ‘s existing partnerships, particularly its agreement with the Chinese Professional Football League, which runs until 2029. Real Madrid face an uncomfortable situation The developments come despite Mbappe issuing a public apology , acknowledging that his comments were ill-judged and expressing regret for the offence caused. The situation is particularly sensitive for Los Blancos because Mbappe is not simply their leading attacker. He is also one of the club’s most recognisable international figures whose commercial appeal transcends markets. However, there is an important distinction between the consequences affecting Mbappe personally and those affecting Madrid. Kylian Mbappe has found himself embroiled in a controversy after El Clasico. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) While several of his sponsorship agreements have ended, it remains unclear whether the controversy could also affect Real Madrid’s commercial partnerships. Tebas has made it clear that an individual controversy should not damage years of cooperation between Spanish football and China. It remains to be seen whether the fallout from this situation can be resolved amicably and things return to normal sooner rather than later.

The teenager hits boundaries at will, and he scores at strike rates that look almost unreal on paper. On Tuesday, his 19-ball 45 in Wellington was another reminder of what he can do when he is sent out to open the batting. He and Abhishek Sharma put together a stand of 133 runs, which set up a six-wicket win for India in Wellington. Sooryavanshi was dismissed after a rampaging knock, but Abhishek stayed on and made a century, scoring 113 off 38 balls, and he was named Player of the Match. In simple terms, Sooryavanshi opens up his hips and pelvis while keeping his upper body and shoulders turned back, so that the muscles around his core are stretched like a loaded spring. He then lets everything go at once, and the bat head swings into the ball at great speed. The energy in that movement travels up through the body in a chain, starting from the ground, passing through the hips and the core, and finally reaching the shoulders and the bat. That is what produces the torque, and it explains why a slim teenager can hit the ball as far as he does. Here is how Karthik described it: "He's got a lot of mechanisms, right, the way he torques, and it's called a shoulder-hip-shoulder separation; they call it in power-hitting. item.description: Mitchell Starc produced a devastating spell to claim his 20th five-wicket haul in Test cricket, helping Australia stage a remarkable comeback against South Africa on the opening day of the deciding third Test at Newlands on Tuesday. He has moved to the top of the list of active fast bowlers with the most five-wicket hauls in Test cricket, ahead of Kagiso Rabada, who has 17, and Jasprit Bumrah, who has 16. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the end of the 2026 MLB season comes more uncertainty than the league has had in a number of years. The expiration of the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) between the owners and players is expected to trigger a lockout, meaning the timeline for baseball is very much up in the air ahead of the 2027 season. With owners pushing for a salary cap and salary floor while players insist they won't budge, the next few months could get messy. The lockout doesn't start the moment the season ends, but the pressure is already on for both sides to start working toward a deal to avoid MLB's most significant work stoppage in decades. Here are the key dates to know for MLB's impending lockout, including when it will begin. MORE: 5 big things to know about impending MLB lockout When does MLB lockout start? MLB is expected to lock out the players upon expiration of the CBA on Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET. While the expiration of the CBA doesn't automatically trigger a lockout, MLB enacting a lockout is simply a formality. That means, until the night of Dec. 1, the offseason can proceed as normal. Once the lockout begins, however, all transactions are halted and teams cannot make contact with any player on their 40-man roster.
